A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FedSPZO and contain readable text, equations, algorithms and experimental displays. All pages were inspected: v2 ends with references without appendices; v3 includes Appendices A–C. Reformatting does not prevent matching corresponding content.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original RoBERTa-large experiments measuring accuracy, computation, memory and communication.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendices A–C report original evaluations across several models and tasks, including ablations and optimizer, adapter and split-placement comparisons.

M1.justification: The defining two-block estimator and activation reuse remain. Algorithms 1–2 revise update/reconstruction handling from one averaged scalar per block to per-perturbation scalars, bringing the pseudocode closer to the existing estimator equations. Appendix B also introduces LoRA/QLoRA variants.

E1.justification: v3 adds MultiRC and SQuAD evaluations, substantially extending the reported task coverage through multi-sentence reading comprehension and question answering. SST-2, RTE, WiC and BoolQ match coverage already listed in v2; BoolQ is not a newly introduced dataset.

E2.justification: v3 retains the principal baselines but adds central-difference no-split controls and an independently perturbed two-block comparator in Section 4.5, plus AdamW variants in Appendix A. FedAvg(LoRA) also enters accuracy comparisons. FedKSeed receives discussion, not a direct evaluation.

E3.justification: New evaluations introduce OPT-1.3B, FP16 LLaMA-3.2-3B, SQuAD F1 evaluation, and controlled perturbation-budget and split-placement settings. Section 4.4 adds training-time estimation assuming 2 MB/s upload and 1280 GFLOPS. The existing 10% client participation and 20 local steps remain.

E4.justification: v2 announces an ablation study but provides no corresponding results. v3 adds no-splitting, perturbation-budget and independent-block tests in Section 4.5, split-placement sensitivity in Appendix C, and optimizer/adapter analyses in Appendices A–B. These directly examine the method's contribution and applicability.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seed schedules, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The perturbation seeds described in the algorithms are method components, not experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive benchmark, ablation, appendix and estimated training-time results. Original RoBERTa computation ratios are retained, but DecomFL's SST-2 accuracy changes from 92.0% in v2 Table 1 to approximately 92.5% in v3 Figure 6, slightly above FedSPZO's retained 92.3%.

T1.justification: v3 Equation (3) corrects the loss-pair summation bounds from 0 through 2Ps in v2 Equation (5) to 1 through 2Ps, consistent with the declared vector length. The central estimator and split-computation formulas remain; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central computational-efficiency contribution remains. The abstract replaces the 1.6–3× reduction claim with up to 3×, the introduction adds ablation-based validation as an explicit contribution, and the conclusion newly states an average 2× reduction.

C2.justification: v3 substantially expands explanations of perturbation-budget diminishing returns, cross-block interactions and split-placement costs. Appendix B explains why adding unquantized LoRA provides no further memory or upload savings. Section 4.3 also moderates v2's accuracy-superiority interpretation to similar accuracy among ZO methods.

D1.justification: New disclosures include LoRA rank 8, scaling 16 and query/value targets, training horizons up to 12K rounds, PyTorch-profiler FLOP measurement and activation-memory accounting. These improve experimental specification but do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: v3 adds references covering QLoRA, AdamW, classical ZO analysis and additional federated finetuning work. It further positions FedKSeed's finite seed pool as orthogonal and discusses a central-difference proxy comparison. The overall computation-focused positioning remains; DecomFL's publication update represents the same work.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, methodology and results receive extensive rewriting and expanded explanation. v3 introduces dedicated training-time and ablation sections and three appendices, rewrites the pseudocode, and standardizes the title terminology to zeroth-order.

P2.justification: v3 changes from two-column to single-column layout, expands Figure 1's annotations and the memory displays, and replaces v2's accuracy table and SST-2 loss curves with broader bar-chart comparisons. Figures 7–13 add substantial ablation and appendix displays.

improvement.justification: Section 4.5 supplies controls missing from v2 that separate splitting benefits from central-versus-forward-difference effects, resolving an important validation gap. Broader model/task evaluations and Appendices A–C strengthen evidence for applicability and design choices. These gains outweigh reduced numerical readability from replacing the accuracy table with bars. Reporting weaknesses remain, including absent run uncertainty and the 2K-scalar communication claim conflicting with the revised algorithms.
